title: Three Positive Numbers
statement: Positive real numbers $x$, $y$ and $z$ satisfy $$\log_{2}(xy)=7,\qquad \log_{2}(yz)=11,\qquad \left|\log_{2}(zx)-6\right|=4.$$ What is the product of all possible values of $xyz$?
hints: Give names to $\log_{2} x$, $\log_{2} y$ and $\log_{2} z$. Which combination of these three numbers tells you the value of $xyz$?

Use the logarithm law $\log_{2}(uv)=\log_{2}u+\log_{2}v$. With $a=\log_{2}x$, $b=\log_{2}y$ and $c=\log_{2}z$, the conditions become linear equations such as $a+b=7$ and $b+c=11$. Since $\log_{2}(xyz)=a+b+c$, try combining the equations to reach this sum directly, without finding $a$, $b$ and $c$ one by one.

With $a$, $b$ and $c$ as the base-$2$ logarithms of $x$, $y$ and $z$, the absolute value condition says that $a+c$ is $10$ or $2$. Adding this to $a+b=7$ and $b+c=11$ gives $2(a+b+c)=28$ or $2(a+b+c)=20$. So $xyz$ is either $2^{14}$ or $2^{10}$, provided each case really occurs. Check that it does, then combine the two values as the question asks.
solution: Since $x$, $y$ and $z$ are positive, we may set $a=\log_{2}x$, $b=\log_{2}y$ and $c=\log_{2}z$. The law $\log_{2}(uv)=\log_{2}u+\log_{2}v$ turns the first two conditions into $a+b=7$ and $b+c=11$, and the third into $|a+c-6|=4$. A number has absolute value $4$ exactly when it equals $4$ or $-4$, so $a+c=10$ or $a+c=2$. We want $xyz$, and $\log_{2}(xyz)=a+b+c$. Each of $a$, $b$ and $c$ appears in exactly two of the three equations, so adding the equations gives $2(a+b+c)=7+11+(a+c)=18+(a+c)$. If $a+c=10$, then $a+b+c=14$. If $a+c=2$, then $a+b+c=10$. Both cases occur. Subtracting each two-variable equation from the sum recovers the remaining variable. In the first case, $(a,b,c)=(3,4,7)$, so $(x,y,z)=(8,16,128)$. Then $xy=2^{7}$, $yz=2^{11}$ and $zx=2^{10}$, and $|10-6|=4$. In the second case, $(a,b,c)=(-1,8,3)$, so $(x,y,z)=\left(\frac{1}{2},256,8\right)$. Then $xy=2^{7}$, $yz=2^{11}$ and $zx=2^{2}$, and $|2-6|=4$. Both triples consist of positive numbers, so both are valid. Hence the possible values of $xyz$ are exactly $2^{14}$ and $2^{10}$, and their product is $2^{24}$. The answer is $16777216$. Why this works. linear-combination-of-equations, log-properties: logarithms turn the products into linear equations, and adding these gives the sum that determines $xyz$ without solving for each variable first.
